evidence: Cic. Att. 11.12.3: sī quis congressus fuerit mihi cum Caesare (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: a friendly meeting, a conference, a conversation; Cicero’s word for a meeting arranged to talk things over. Traupman gives it for a meeting, a conference and a congress.

evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.4.107: celeberrimō virōrum mulierumque conventū (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: For a larger gathering, not a few colleagues round a table.

evidence: Caes. BG 1.43: eō ad colloquium vēnērunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A talk between two sides; the lexicon’s word for an interview.

phrases.latin: sī quis congressus fuerit mihi cum Caesare
phrases.english: if I have any meeting with Caesar

sources: Lewis & Short: congressus · Lewis & Short: conventus · Lewis & Short: colloquium
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 344, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).
